implemented.escape: kk._jsonEscape VALUE -> RESULT: fork-free; fast path = one glob (__KK_JSON_SPECIAL = *["\\<U+0001>-<U+001F>]*); slow path: backslash first, then quote, then per control code present one global replace from a 31-entry table (\n \r \t \b \f named, the rest \u00xx lower-case); DEL/C1/multibyte raw
implemented.toJSON_body: if [[ "${state[*]}" != ${__KK_JSON_SPECIAL:-*} ]]; then printf '%s\n' "{...${state[p]-}...}"; else kk._jsonObject C p "${state[p]-}" ...; fi — ONE glob over the whole instance store; the printed values are exactly the tested ones (read from <inst>_data, not via the per-property namerefs), so a clean verdict cannot be wrong; a class with a property named `state` binds its own local -n __kk_d="${this}_data" instead
implemented.fromJSON: kk._jsonParse TEXT fills the caller's local __kk_jk/__kk_jv (+ __kk_jc/__kk_jhc for __class__); members without a backslash consumed by one anchored ERE (__KK_JSON_RE_MEMBER), everything else by the scanner (kk._jsonString), which alone decides acceptance; one-pass unescape of \" \\ \/ \b \f \n \r \t and \uXXXX; UTF-8 bytes built arithmetically via printf \xHH; parse-all-then-assign = atomic; output written to <inst>_data (state[p]); prints the instance name on success (unchanged)
implemented.tables: kk._jsonInit builds __KK_JSON_CC/ESC/SPECIAL/CTRL/WS/RE_MEMBER with printf only (no $'..' in any function body: declare -f/export -f re-print those bytes raw and a raw CR is lost — measured); called at load and lazily by every helper (child shell with only the exported functions)
implemented.exports: export -f adds kk._jsonInit kk._jsonEscape kk._jsonObject kk._jsonString kk._jsonParse (module exports unconditionally, as before)

measured: printf '\uXXXX' (both bashes): BMP -> UTF-8 in C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8 AND C; a lone surrogate (\ud83d / \udc00) -> CESU bytes ed a0 bd / ed b0 80 (invalid UTF-8) in the UTF-8 locales and the literal text \uD83D in C; a pair in ONE printf is combined (f0 9f 98 80) in all three locales; \U0001f600 -> UTF-8 in the UTF-8 locales but LITERAL in C; \u0000 truncates everything after it. Hence: pairs combined, lone surrogates rc 1, bytes built arithmetically via \xHH (locale-independent)
patsub_replacement is ON by default on both bashes: an unquoted & in a ${v//p/r} replacement is the match; every replacement here is a quoted variable
the fast-path glob *["\\<01>-<1F>]* gives identical verdicts in C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8 on both bashes for 16 probes (DEL and U+0085 miss)
declare -f re-prints $'..' words with raw bytes and a raw CR does not survive (both bashes) -> no $'..' in function bodies; tables built with printf at load

MSYS/cygwin quirk (both bashes): a CR inside $'..' is DROPPED in a compound array assignment — a=($'x\ry') gives 'xy'; a simple assignment and a command argument keep it. Test 131 builds its CR fixtures by expansion and pins the fixture length
a statement in a method body costs ~10-12 us on the 1000-instance bench shell; bash re-compiles a [[ =~ ]] regex on every evaluation (the 6-group member ERE: ~25 us per match on 5.2)
the bench class's fromJSON: old here-string parser 1285-1420 us -> new 853-958 us
deviations: __class__ rule: accepts the receiving instance's class OR the serializer's class (plan: 'mismatch with the receiving instance's class'); needed for a subclass inheriting the serializer to read its own toJSON output (pinned by test 131). An unrelated class is refused.
\uXXXX is decoded by arithmetic UTF-8 encoding through printf \xHH, not printf \uXXXX: printf \U / lone \u are locale-dependent (measured above); the result is identical where printf \u works

toJSON reads (and fromJSON writes) the instance store <inst>_data directly instead of the per-property namerefs: identical cells for plain/computed/lazy properties; it makes the single-expansion guard airtight (a static property shadowing a serialized name can no longer slip an unescaped value past the check) and is part of the perf fix
a member-level ERE fast path in front of the scanner (perf); the scanner alone decides acceptance; the ERE only matches members without a backslash, so it decodes nothing
raw control characters inside an input string are accepted (lenient; JSON forbids them, the old parser accepted them, loadObjects cannot deliver a raw LF anyway)
kk._jsonEscape returns through RESULT (kcl §1.1); the generated toJSON restores the caller's RESULT as every method does
